newsitem.title: POLAND: FAST-TRACK FINES FOR SOCCER THUGS IN POLAND.
newsitem.headline: FAST-TRACK FINES FOR SOCCER THUGS IN POLAND.

text.p: Poland has arranged for misdemeanours courts to hand down instant sentences against hooligans during or immediately after Sunday's World Cup soccer qualifier against Moldova in the southern city of Katowice.

PAP news agency said on Friday that Justice Minister Leszek Kubicki had granted a request by Katowice's governor to temporarily introduce the fast-track penalties on Saturday and Sunday, after first refusing.

The police will effectively act as prosecutors and whisk hooligans in front of the magistrates the moment they commit such offenses as disturbing the peace, destroying property, are caught carrying dangerous objects or shooting off fireworks.
PAP said the minister had granted permission after the governor sent an account of battles among fans at a recent ice-hockey match and a rise in violence at local sports events.
"In changing his mind, the minister recognised that there was a justified reasons for introducing a rapid sentencing procedure," Kubicki's spokeswoman Barbara Makosa-Stepkowska told the agency.
Poland has got tough on soccer hooliganism following a spate of such incidents -- shutting one major stadium until next year and installing video cameras at others.
